what: Edwards Lifesciences makes heart valves and the catheters used to place them. Its transcatheter aortic valve, placed through an artery rather than open surgery, is the product it is best known for.
money: replacement aortic valves delivered by catheter
newer valve repair and replacement devices
Surgical Structural Heart and Critical Care
moat: Two decades of clinical trial evidence that regulators and insurers rely on, and physician training that makes its delivery systems familiar.
risks: Growth in aortic valves has slowed as the market matures
Competitors are approved in the same procedures
Hospital capacity limits how many procedures can be done
Reimbursement decisions determine which patients qualify
opportunities: Mitral and tricuspid valve therapy is a large, barely treated market
Expanding approvals to patients with milder disease widens the eligible population
It holds about $4.6 billion of cash against almost no debt
watch: Transcatheter aortic valve growth and the launch pace of mitral and tricuspid devices.
